question: Which day is recognised as International Youth Day in 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**August 12**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **International Youth Day** is observed annually on **August 12** across the globe to recognize the efforts of the world's youth in enhancing global society.
 
• The **United Nations General Assembly (UNGA)** officially designated this day in **December 1999**, following recommendations made by the **World Conference of Ministers Responsible for Youth** held in **Lisbon** in **August 1998**.
 
• The very first International Youth Day was celebrated on **August 12, 2000**, serving as an opportunity for governments and others to draw attention to youth issues worldwide.
 
• The observance aims to promote ways to engage young people in becoming more actively involved in making positive contributions to their communities and participating in **social, economic, and political life**.
 
• Each year, the **United Nations** selects a specific theme for the day; for example, the **2024** theme was **"From Clicks to Progress: Youth Digital Pathways for Sustainable Development,"** highlighting the role of digitalization in achieving **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **National Youth Day (India):**
 
 
• In **India**, **National Youth Day** is celebrated on **January 12** every year.
 
• This date was chosen to honor the birth anniversary of **Swami Vivekananda**, one of India's greatest spiritual and social leaders, who had immense faith in the power of youth.
 
• The government of India declared this day as National Youth Day in **1984**, and it was first celebrated in **1985**.
 
 
 
• **Defining "Youth":**
 
 
• The **United Nations** defines "youth" as those persons between the ages of **15 and 24** years for statistical purposes without prejudice to other definitions by **Member States**.
 
• Currently, there are **1.2 billion** young people aged **15 to 24** years, accounting for **16 percent** of the global population.
 
• By **2030**—the target date for the **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**—the number of youth is projected to have grown by **7 percent**, to nearly **1.3 billion**.
 
 
 
• **Global Initiatives:**
 
 
• The **UN Youth Strategy (Youth2030)** was launched in **2018** to facilitate increased impact and expanded action to address the needs of young people.
 
• The **Economic and Social Council (ECOSOC)** Youth Forum is an annual event that provides a platform for young people to engage in a dialogue with **Member States** on global policy.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Other Important Dates:**
 
 
• **August 9:** Observed as the **International Day of the World's Indigenous Peoples**.
 
• **September 21:** Recognized as the **International Day of Peace** (World Peace Day).
 
• **July 18:** Celebrated as **Nelson Mandela International Day** to honor the legacy of the former South African President.
 
 
 
• **Thematic Focus:** International Youth Day often focuses on critical areas such as **education**, **employment**, **environment**, **mental health**, and **civic engagement** to empower the younger generation for a better future.
